name: Diode laser hair removal (LightSheer)

card.summary: The common 800-810 nm clinic hair-removal laser; LightSheer is a widely used brand with registered clinical trials.
card.note: Reduction rather than guaranteed permanent removal; pigment changes are a recognised risk.

quick.overview:
Diode lasers emit near-infrared light around 800-810 nm that melanin absorbs, and are among the most common clinic hair-removal devices. LightSheer is a diode laser line, with registered trials of its handpieces for hair reduction.

Wikipedia notes a randomized trial where diode laser reduced hair by 69.2 percent at 12 months versus 52.7 percent for IPL.
quick.mechanism: Selective photothermolysis: light is absorbed by melanin in the hair, heating the follicle, while skin cooling protects the surface. Only growing follicles are affected, so sessions repeat every few weeks.
quick.risks: Short-term redness, swelling and pain are common; burns and pigment changes are possible. A 2006 review described by Wikipedia reported side effects in 28.9 percent for diode versus 9.5 percent for alexandrite.

lead: Diode laser hair removal uses semiconductor lasers around 800 to 810 nm to reduce hair by heating melanin in the follicle. Wikipedia lists pulsed diode arrays (810 nm) as suited to pale to medium skin. [1]
LightSheer is a diode hair-removal system whose handpieces (such as LightSheer Duet HS and ET) have been the subject of registered clinical studies. [2][3][4][5]
Wikipedia describes a randomized trial in which diode laser produced 69.2 percent hair reduction at 12 months, versus 52.7 percent for IPL. [1]

paras: The laser is absorbed by melanin and heats the follicle; spot size, fluence, pulse width and cooling all affect results and side effects. [1]
Most people need at least eight sessions spaced three to eight weeks apart, according to Wikipedia, and the FDA defines "permanent" as long-term stable reduction rather than total removal. [1]

A 2006 review described on Wikipedia reported side effects in 28.9 percent for diode lasers versus 9.5 percent for alexandrite and 15.3 percent for IPL. [1] Common effects include redness and swelling; serious effects include acne flares, burns and skin discoloration. [1]

ClinicalTrials.gov lists completed LightSheer studies: a hair-count reduction verification of the Duet HS handpiece (NCT01282866, n=35) [2], a comparison of two 810 nm diode lasers for hypertrichosis (NCT01212172, n=20) [3], an evaluation of the 805 nm Duet HS handpiece (NCT01801202, n=21) [4], and a comparison of HS versus ET handpieces (NCT00657085, n=5) [5]. Results are not summarised here.
